title: Sheen's menu bar panel
question: Three ways to lay out the menu bar panel in Sheen's design. Pick the one that reads best at a glance.

options.label: Headline and bars
options.thesis: One big light figure says how your Mac is doing; three slim bars give the rest.
options.viewport: Free disk space as a 46pt light figure beside a small glass orb, then CPU, memory and battery bars, one tip, and the Open Sheen pill.
options.risk: Disk space leads even when the CPU is the busy one, unless the headline follows whatever needs attention.

options.label: Tabs
options.thesis: Health, Tips and Devices each get their own tab, so the panel stays short.
options.viewport: A segmented control under the wordmark; Health shows four tiles with light figures and bars, then the network line and the pill.
options.risk: Tips hide behind a tab, so a glance can miss one that matters.

options.label: Glass rings
options.thesis: CPU, memory and disk as three nested glass rings around a status core.
options.viewport: A 150pt ring cluster beside a three-row legend, then free space, battery and network chips, one tip, and the pill.
options.risk: Rings show proportion well but exact numbers live in the legend, one look away.
